items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mr. Farletti presented us to the assistant manager who was an Indian named D.R. Banerjee who was to look after us personally.

ctx.x: The "Taj" was a very large and beautiful place which sat on a street overlooking the bay. The front faces the city and I learned later that the architect that drew the plans for the hotel commited suicide after the hotel was completed because the back of the hotel was built facing the bay and it should have been the opposite.

I had a very large room assigned to me in the hotel until other lodgings could be arranged. The bed was very large also and had cheesecloth curtains on the four sides which was to keep the mosquitos from having a good time when you went to sleep at night. Mr. Farletti presented us to the assistant manager who was an Indian named D.R. Banerjee who was to look after us personally.

On the left side of the Taj facing the bay was a monument called the Gateway to India and to the left of that was a smaller hotel owned by the Taj direction called the Mayfair. I also met a pianist and accordionist called Teddy Weatherford. Teddy was an American Negro who had travelled over most of the Far East and had a big name amongst the early jazz musicians before I came on the scene.
